assessment_summary:
I inspected the checked-out repo at /workspace (commit d170d74) and the running Docker state. The final installation method per the summary is the base docker-compose.yml combined with a sandbox-only docker-compose.override.yml that resets deploy.resources.limits; I confirmed the override exists, that Compose loads both files (container labels list both config_files), and that the four services are running with the guide's exact host port bindings. I then validated actual software behavior rather than mere file existence.

Behavioral checks: the web health endpoint returns {\"ok\":true} (HTTP 200); the public portal renders under Host: urbankit.de (307 -> /de -> HTTP 200, correct title/content); the workspace root under Host: app.urbankit.de redirects to /dashboard and lands on the login page (HTTP 200), matching the guide's domain-splitting middleware; /admin and /de/register render; the unauthenticated /api/users call returns 403, proving Payload is connected to MongoDB and enforcing auth; the public /api/projects and /api/globals/platform-settings endpoints return HTTP 200 with seeded global data. MongoDB contains the full urban_kit schema (29 collections). The hocuspocus sidecar logs 'Ready', its PAYLOAD_INTERNAL_URL points to http://web:3000, it can fetch the web health endpoint successfully, and a raw WebSocket handshake returns 101 Switching Protocols with a valid accept key. The NEXT_PUBLIC_HOCUSPOCUS_URL build arg is verifiably baked into the client bundle. The Next.js server started cleanly (Ready in 745ms) with no error-level logs other than expected 403 auth denials.

Limitations/uncertainty: the host lacks ss/netstat, so listening sockets were confirmed indirectly via Docker port mappings and successful connections to 127.0.0.1:3020/1234/8025/27019. The production override (docker-compose.prod.yml) and demo-account seeding were not exercised; the guide lists these as optional for running the stack, and the empty users collection is expected since the deployment path runs no seeding or migrations. The initial unmodified compose run that failed was an abandoned attempt blocked by a host cgroup v2 threaded-mode limitation (environmental), not an incomplete installation. On that basis the installation is complete and operational.
